cards.explanation: The answer is the spirit of a destroyer. The LORD says, "Behold, I will stir up against Babylon and against the people of Leb-kamai the spirit of a destroyer." (Jeremiah 51:1) Not a famine and not a plague, but a destroyer. The target and the destroyer are both right there in the verse.

The answer is True. The LORD says strangers will come against Babylon "…from every side in her day of disaster." (Jeremiah 51:2) They come to winnow her and empty her land. Winnowing is tossing grain so the wind blows the chaff away, and I think that picture is a rough one for Babylon.

The word is spare. The orders say, "Do not spare her young men; devote all her army to destruction!" (Jeremiah 51:3) It's a heavy line, friends, and I think it's okay to just let it be heavy. The LORD is speaking about Babylon's army here.

The answer is False. The LORD says Israel and Judah "…have not been abandoned by their God, the LORD of Hosts, though their land is full of guilt before the Holy One of Israel." (Jeremiah 51:5) Both things are in the same verse. The guilt is named, and so is the LORD not abandoning them.

The reason is that it is the time of the LORD's vengeance. The call says, "Flee from Babylon! Escape with your lives! Do not be destroyed in her punishment. For this is the time of the LORD’s vengeance; He will pay her what she deserves." (Jeremiah 51:6) The reason is right there in the verse.

The word is drunk. "Babylon was a gold cup in the hand of the LORD, making the whole earth drunk." (Jeremiah 51:7) It's a picture, not a recipe, friends. Then the verse says, "The nations drank her wine; therefore the nations have gone mad."

The call is to wail for her and get her balm. The text says, "Wail for her; get her balm for her pain; perhaps she can be healed." (Jeremiah 51:8) Balm is a soothing ointment for a wound. That line has some tenderness in it, and I think it's worth noticing.

The answer is False. The text says, "We tried to heal Babylon, but she could not be healed." (Jeremiah 51:9) They give it a real effort, and she still can't be healed. That's why the next words are, "Abandon her!"

What they tell is what the LORD our God has accomplished. The call says, "The LORD has brought forth our vindication; come, let us tell in Zion what the LORD our God has accomplished." (Jeremiah 51:10) The telling is about what the LORD did. It's good news to share.

The reason is that His plan is to destroy Babylon. "The LORD has aroused the spirit of the kings of the Medes, because His plan is aimed at Babylon to destroy her…" (Jeremiah 51:11) The LORD stirs the kings of the Medes for this plan. The reason is stated right in the verse.

The answer is True. The verse says, "…the LORD has both devised and accomplished what He spoke against the people of Babylon." (Jeremiah 51:12) Planned and carried out, both in one verse. What He spoke is what He did.

What has come for her is her end. The verse says, "You who dwell by many waters, rich in treasures, your end has come; the thread of your life is cut." (Jeremiah 51:13) Waterfront and wealthy, and still her end comes. A hard line, and the text just says it plainly.

The word is shout. The LORD of Hosts says, "Surely I will fill you up with men as with locusts, and they will shout in triumph over you." (Jeremiah 51:14) And He swore it by Himself. That's as solid as a promise gets.

The word is breath. The verse says the goldsmith's "…molten images are a fraud, and there is no breath in them." (Jeremiah 51:17) A goldsmith works metal, and the idol still has no life in it. Meanwhile the LORD is the One who "…brings forth the wind from His storehouses." (Jeremiah 51:16)

What happens to the idols is that they will perish. "They are worthless, a work to be mocked. In the time of their punishment they will perish." (Jeremiah 51:18) The verse calls the idols worthless. Then it says what happens to them: they perish.

The word is shatters. The LORD says, "You are My war club, My weapon for battle. With you I shatter nations; with you I bring kingdoms to ruin." (Jeremiah 51:20) The text doesn't name who the war club is, so I won't guess, friends. It just says what the LORD does with it.

He repays them for all the evil they did in Zion. The LORD says, "Before your very eyes I will repay Babylon and all the dwellers of Chaldea for all the evil they have done in Zion…" (Jeremiah 51:24) The reason is stated right there. The verse names where the evil was done: Zion.

The answer is False. The LORD says, "No one shall retrieve from you a cornerstone or a foundation stone, because you will become desolate forever…" (Jeremiah 51:26) Not even the stones that hold a building up get taken. That's how complete it is.
